items.title: One week left to comment on the IASB's risk mitigation accounting proposals
items.summary: The extended comment period on the IASB Exposure Draft Risk Mitigation Accounting, which proposes amendments to IFRS 9 and IFRS 7, closes on 30 November 2026.
detail: The IASB published the Exposure Draft in December 2025. It proposes a new accounting model to reflect how financial institutions manage interest rate risk, with amendments to IFRS 9 and to the IFRS 7 disclosure requirements.
In May 2026 the Board extended the comment deadline to 30 November 2026. The IASB will then analyse the feedback before deciding how to finalise the model.
items.why: Risk mitigation accounting is the biggest open IFRS 9 project and a likely topic in advanced financial instruments units.

items.title: Bitcoin holds near US$60,800 after a weekend rebound
items.summary: Bitcoin traded at US$60,773 on Crypto.com Exchange late on 22 November UTC, up 1.25% over 24 hours, while Ether rose 1.92% to US$1,714.
detail: Bitcoin's 24-hour range ran from US$58,641 to US$61,577, with about 5,746 BTC (around US$345 million) traded on the exchange. Ether traded between US$1,645 and US$1,730.

Solana slipped 0.45% to US$70.37 and Tether stayed close to its dollar peg at US$0.9987. The moves follow the previous day's gains of more than 5% for Bitcoin, after a week in which the S&P 500 fell 3.7%.
items.why: Crypto prices feed straight into the fair value and impairment questions behind the IASB's new cryptoasset project.

items.title: OECD publishes Action 14 peer reviews of 18 jurisdictions
items.summary: On 19 November 2026 the OECD released Cycle 1 full peer review reports on how 18 jurisdictions apply the BEPS Action 14 minimum standard on mutual agreement procedures (MAP).
detail: According to KPMG's summary, Ireland, Japan, Latvia, Luxembourg, Malta, Morocco and the United States meet almost all elements of the standard, and Austria, Denmark, Finland, France, Malaysia and Norway meet most of them. About one third of US tax treaties are not fully aligned with the standard, and the reports flag issues with timely implementation of MAP agreements.

The reviews follow the OECD's 2025 MAP statistics, released on Tax Certainty Day on 4 November: competent authorities closed a record 2,971 cases in 2025, up 17.6% on 2024, and average closing time fell from 27.37 to 25.66 months. The OECD will keep publishing peer reviews in batches.
items.why: Action 14 is the treaty dispute resolution backbone for transfer pricing cases, central to your MAP and tax disputes interests.

items.title: India's extended return deadline for audit cases passed on 21 November
items.summary: India's CBDT had moved the income tax return due date for specified audit cases for AY 2026-27 from 31 October to 21 November 2026; companies with transfer pricing cases file by 30 November.
detail: The extension came through CBDT Circular 07/2026 of 28 September 2026. Several other forms, such as Forms 10E and 10-EE, were also due on 21 November, which fell on a Saturday.

Taxpayers with international or specified domestic transactions with associated enterprises sit on a separate track: a company with even one such transaction files by 30 November together with its transfer pricing report.
items.why: India's separate TP filing track shows how domestic compliance calendars are built around transfer pricing documentation.

items.title: PIIE warns the Miami G20 summit may collapse, with tax cooperation off the agenda
items.summary: A Peterson Institute analysis says the US presidency has rejected international tax cooperation, climate, trade and anti-corruption as objectives for the G20 leaders' summit in Miami on 14 and 15 December 2026.
detail: The piece notes that South African president Cyril Ramaphosa has been disinvited, which breaks the G20 troika process that links one presidency to the next.

It suggests other leaders might draft an alternative declaration, which could produce a split summit. The OECD's Secretary-General Tax Report to G20 finance ministers was published on 15 October 2026.
items.why: G20 political backing has driven Pillar One and Two, so a summit without tax cooperation weakens momentum on the global minimum tax.

items.title: Rupiah down 8.4% in 2026 as BI points to global pressure
items.summary: Bank Indonesia said the rupiah has weakened about 8.4% so far in 2026 and pointed to global conditions, after raising the BI-Rate 25 bps to 6.00% on 18 November.
detail: Bisnis.com reported BI's comments on 19 November. Analysts quoted by Bisnis say the Fed and the dollar index have had a larger influence on the rupiah recently, and that net capital outflows reached US$740 million between 15 October and 10 November 2026.
A Bisnis forecast put the rupiah between Rp18,100 and Rp18,400 per US dollar this week, with a risk of a slide toward Rp18,500 by the end of November. JISDOR stood at Rp18,269 on 19 November.
items.why: A weaker rupiah raises foreign currency translation and debt-servicing issues under PSAK for Indonesian companies with dollar borrowings.

items.title: DJP steps up tax supervision to lift year-end revenue
items.summary: DDTCNews reports the Directorate General of Taxes is strengthening supervision and enforcement in the final weeks of 2026 to close the gap to its revenue target.
detail: The DJP is leaning on monitoring and collection measures, including the 0.5% PPh Pasal 22 that four designated marketplaces now withhold on merchants' gross turnover.
Kemenkeu still needs roughly Rp500 trillion in tax in November and December. The push comes as the BI-Rate rise to 6.00% adds pressure on business cash flow.
items.why: Year-end enforcement drives SP2DK letters, audits and later disputes at the Tax Court.

worth.title: OECD publishes Action 14 peer reviews of 18 jurisdictions
worth.text: The new MAP peer reviews, read alongside the record 2,971 MAP closures in 2025, give a clear picture of where treaty dispute resolution works and where it still stalls, which is useful for any transfer pricing or tax disputes assignment.
